newsitem.title: USA: Simpson struck ex-wife - witnesses testify.
newsitem.headline: Simpson struck ex-wife - witnesses testify.

text.p: (Note language in 15th graf)
By Steve James
O.J. Simpson's best friend testified on Tuesday that Nicole Brown Simpson told him the former football star hit her and two other witnesses said they saw Simpson slap her.
The civil trial testimony contradicted Simpson's statement last week that he had never hit her.

Al Cowlings, who grew up with Simpson and was driving the Ford Bronco in which Simpson led police on a slow-speed chase June 17, 1994, before being arrested, reluctantly told lawyers for the plaintiffs about an incident on New Year's Day 1989.
Woken in the night, he went to the Simpsons' home and saw an "upset" Nicole Brown Simpson. "She had told me that she was hit. Yes," Cowlings said.
Asked if it was Simpson who had hit her, he replied: "Yes, she probably did." Pressed by attorney John Kelly if that was what she told him, Cowlings replied "Yes."

Later, showed photographs of a bruised and battered Nicole Brown Simpson, whom he had said he loved as a sister, Cowlings dabbed at his eyes and appeared shaken. He interrupted a question from Kelly to take a sip of water, prompting Kelly to ask if he was all right.
Cowlings said he had taken her to the hospital emergency room that night, because she was complaining of a headache and he was worried she might have concussion.

Simpson, who Cowlings said was his "closest and dearest friend," was acquitted in criminal court in October last year of murdering his ex-wife and her friend Ronald Goldman. He has been sued in civil court by the victims' families for "wrongful death".
As the trial resumed after a holiday weekend, plaintiffs' attorneys meanwhile indicated another of Simpson's long-time friends, lawyer Robert Kardashian would not testify for them.
Kardashian, who cited attorney-client privilege for not testifying at Simpson's criminal trial, has since said publicly he has doubts about Simpson's innocence.
Kelly said Kardashian had promised to testify but at the last moment had declined, unless subpoenaed. Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki declined a motion to force Kardashian to testify.

Simpson testified last week that he had never struck his ex- wife. But in testimony on Tuesday, India Rose Allen, a former nude model, said she had seen Simpson slap Nicole Brown Simpson at a Beverly Hills veterinarian's office where Allen worked in 1983.
She said Simpson's then wife came to collect her dogs wearing a gold Spandex exercise outfit with a full-length fur coat over the top.
Simpson drove up as she was leaving and "he was mad, gritting his teeth and with his fists clenched."
Allen said Simpson confronted his wife and said: 'I didn't buy this coat for you to go fuck someone else. I want the coat back.'

"He tried to pull it off her, she jerked away from him and he struck her across the face. Her sunglasses and headband went flying and she had a fading bruise under her eye," the former Playboy Playmate said.
In later testimony, Albert Aguilera, who once lived in Laguna Beach where the Simpsons had rented a beach house, recalled an incident around July 4th 1986, in which he saw Simpson hit his wife.
He said he was walking with a friend in the surf and saw Simpson and Nicole Brown Simpson around 50 yards (46 metres) ahead on the beach.
"It appeared she was teasing him. She was standing in front of him with her back to the sea, he was facing the water.

"Suddenly he slapped her and she fell down. He swung his right hand and she went down," said Aguilera, who said he was at the University of Southern California the same time Simpson was a star running back there.
Earlier in the day, Judge Fujisaki instructed the jury to disregard lie detector test testimony from Simpson.
He said plaintiffs' lawyer Daniel Petrocelli had asked Simpson whether he had failed a polygraph test and that he has scored a minus 22, which Petrocelli said indicated "extreme deception."
Citing attorney-client privilege, Fujisaki also said questions by a lawyer did not constitute evidence.
"You must totally disregard the questions about taking lie detector tests, test scores and their meanings and treat the subject as if you had never heard of it," the judge said.
